title: Zariski's Main Theorem for a monogenic algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R[X]$ an ideal of the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $S=R[X]/I$, an $R$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal such that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], and let $S'\subseteq S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then there is $g\in S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the map $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, of localizations at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] induced by the inclusion $S'\subseteq S$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, line 30735; its proof uses Lemma 00PQ)

proof.text:
*Notation.* Let $\varphi:R	o S$ be the structure map, $\pi:R[X]	o S$ the quotient map [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $x=\pi(X)$. Every element of $S$ is $\pi(\sum_ir_iX^i)=\sum_i\varphi(r_i)x^i$ with $r_i\in R$, so $S$ is generated by $x$ as an $R$-algebra (and $R	o S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]). For $r\in R$, $\varphi(r)$ is a root of the monic polynomial $T-\varphi(r)$, so $\varphi(R)\subseteq S'$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; $S'$ is a subring of $S$. Let $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $R$; for $a\in R$, $\varphi(a)
otin\mathfrak q$ iff $a
otin\mathfrak p$. For $m\ge0$ call a tuple $(b_0,\dots,b_m)$ of elements of $S'$ a *relation of length $m$* if $b_0+b_1x+\dots+b_mx^m=0$ in $S$, and *good* if $b_j
otin\mathfrak q$ for some $j$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, lines 30745-30781), first sentence and notation

proof.text: *$S'$ is integrally closed in $S$.* If $t\in S$ is integral over $S'$ (for the inclusion $S'\to S$) then $t\in S'$. Indeed $S'[t]$ is generated as an $S'$-algebra by one element integral over $S'$, so it is a finitely generated $S'$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators], hence integral over $S'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; $S'$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], so $S'[t]$ is integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]; thus $t$ is integral over $R$, i.e. $t\in S'$. (The source uses this implicitly when it writes $b_mx\in S'$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, lines 30745-30781), the assertion '$b_mx\in S'$' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *The top coefficient times $x$ lies in $S'$.* If $(b_0,\dots,b_m)$ is a relation of length $m$, then $b_mx\in S'$: by [lem-weil-pbc-leading-coefficient-times-root-integral] applied to the inclusion $S'\to S$, $t=x$ and $a_j=b_j$, the element $b_mx$ is integral over $S'$, hence lies in $S'$ by step 2.

proof.text: *The fibre ring when $I\subseteq\mathfrak p[X]$.* Assume (H): every $f=\sum_ia_iX^i\in I$ has all $a_i\in\mathfrak p$. Let $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=S\otimes_R\kappa$ the fibre ring, a $\kappa$-algebra through $\iota_\kappa:c\mapsto1\otimes c$, with $\iota_S:s\mapsto s\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. We show $F\cong\kappa[X]$ as $\kappa$-algebras with $x\otimes1\mapsto X$. Let $\psi:R[X]\to\kappa[X]$ apply $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa$ to the coefficients [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. An element $a\in\mathfrak p$ maps to $a/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, i.e. to $0$ in $\kappa$; so by (H) $\psi(I)=0$ and $\psi$ induces an $R$-algebra map $\bar\psi:S\to\kappa[X]$ with $\bar\psi(x)=X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2), with $A=S$, $B=\kappa$, $C=\kappa[X]$, $f=\bar\psi$ and $g$ the inclusion of constants, there is an $R$-algebra map $\alpha:F\to\kappa[X]$ with $\alpha(s\otimes c)=c\,\bar\psi(s)$; $\alpha\circ\iota_\kappa=g$, so $\alpha$ is $\kappa$-linear. Let $\beta:\kappa[X]\to F$ be the $\kappa$-algebra map with $\beta(X)=x\otimes1$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $\alpha\circ\beta$ is a $\kappa$-algebra endomorphism of $\kappa[X]$ fixing $X$, hence the identity. And $\beta\circ\alpha$ is an $R$-algebra endomorphism of $F$ with $\beta\alpha\iota_\kappa(c)=\beta(c)=1\otimes c=\iota_\kappa(c)$ and, for $s=\sum_i\varphi(r_i)x^i$, $\beta\alpha\iota_S(s)=\beta(\sum_i\bar r_iX^i)=\sum_i(1\otimes\bar r_i)(x\otimes1)^i=\sum_i\varphi(r_i)x^i\otimes1=\iota_S(s)$ ($\bar r_i$ the image of $r_i$ in $\kappa$, and $x^i\otimes\bar r_i=r_ix^i\otimes1$ in the tensor product over $R$); by part (3) of the same node $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_F$. So $\alpha:F\to\kappa[X]$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, lines 30745-30781), 'otherwise the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ would be $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *A good relation exists.* Suppose (H) of step 4 holds, and let $\alpha:F\cong\kappa[X]$ be the isomorphism of step 4. Since $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], the prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}\subset F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is isolated in $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A ring isomorphism induces a homeomorphism of spectra ($Q\mapsto\alpha^{-1}(Q)$ maps $D(h)$ onto $D(\alpha^{-1}(h))$), so $Q_0=\alpha(\bar{\mathfrak q})$ is a prime of $\kappa[X]$ with $\{Q_0\}$ open in $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[X]$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-strongly-transcendental-not-quasi-finite] to the subring $\kappa\subseteq\kappa[X]$ and the element $X$: both rings are reduced, $\kappa[X]$ being a domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]; $X$ is strongly transcendental over $\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-strongly-transcendental], since $u\cdot P(X)=0$ in the domain $\kappa[X]$ gives $u=0$ or $P=0$, and in both cases $ua_i=0$ for all coefficients $a_i$ of $P$; and $\kappa[X]$ is generated by $1$ as a module over $\kappa[X]$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Hence $\kappa\to\kappa[X]$ is not quasi-finite at $Q_0$. But the only prime of the field $\kappa$ is $0$, its residue field is $\kappa_{(0)}/0=\kappa$ (all nonzero elements are already units) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the fibre ring $\kappa[X]\otimes_\kappa\kappa$ is identified with $\kappa[X]$ by $j:P\mapsto P\otimes1$ (inverse $P\otimes c\mapsto cP$), and the prime of the fibre corresponding to $Q_0$ is $j(Q_0)$, isolated because $\{Q_0\}$ is; so $\kappa\to\kappa[X]$ is quasi-finite at $Q_0$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], a contradiction. Therefore (H) fails: there is $f=a_0+a_1X+\dots+a_nX^n\in I$ with $a_i\notin\mathfrak p$ for some $i$. Then $(\varphi(a_0),\dots,\varphi(a_n))$ is a relation of length $n$ (its entries lie in $S'$ by step 1, and $\sum_j\varphi(a_j)x^j=\pi(f)=0$), and it is good because $\varphi(a_i)\notin\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: *The inductive claim and its base.* For $m\ge0$ let $C(m)$ be: *for every good relation of length $m$ there is $g\in S'$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, such that $S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^k\mapsto y/g^k$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], is an isomorphism.* We prove $C(m)$ for all $m$ by induction. $C(0)$ holds vacuously: a relation of length $0$ is $b_0=0$, and $0\in\mathfrak q$, so it is not good.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00Q8 (lemma-quasi-finite-monogenic, lines 30745-30781), 'We prove the lemma by induction on $m$. The base case $m=0$ is vacuous'

proof.text:
*Induction step, case $b_m
otin\mathfrak q$.* Let $m\ge1$, assume $C(m-1)$, and let $(b_0,\dots,b_m)$ be a good relation with $b_m
otin\mathfrak q$. Put $g=b_m\in S'$; by step 3, $c=b_mx\in S'$. The map $S'_g	o S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is injective: if $y/g^k\mapsto0$ then $g^ly=0$ in $S$ for some $l$, hence in $S'$, so $y/g^k=0$ in $S'_g$. It is surjective: an element of $S_g$ is $s/g^k$ with $s=\sum_{i=0}^N\varphi(r_i)x^i$ (step 1), and $s/g^k= ig(\sum_{i=0}^N\varphi(r_i)c^ig^{N-i} ig)/g^{N+k}$ with numerator in $S'$ ($\varphi(r_i)\in S'$ by step 1, $c,g\in S'$). So $S'_g	o S_g$ is an isomorphism, and $g
otin\mathfrak q$.

proof.text:
*Induction step, case $b_m\in\mathfrak q$.* Let $m\ge1$, assume $C(m-1)$, and let $(b_0,\dots,b_m)$ be a good relation with $b_m\in\mathfrak q$. By step 3, $c=b_mx\in S'$, and $c\in\mathfrak q$ since $b_m\in\mathfrak q$. Put $b'_{m-1}=c+b_{m-1}\in S'$ ($S'$ is a subring [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]). Then $b_0+\dots+b_{m-2}x^{m-2}+b'_{m-1}x^{m-1}=\sum_{j=0}^mb_jx^j=0$, so $(b_0,\dots,b_{m-2},b'_{m-1})$ is a relation of length $m-1$. It is good: some $b_j
otin\mathfrak q$ and $j
e m$; if $j\le m-2$ this entry is unchanged, and if $j=m-1$ then $b'_{m-1}=b_{m-1}+c
otin\mathfrak q$ since $c\in\mathfrak q$. By $C(m-1)$ there is the required $g$. This completes the induction.

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 5 there is a good relation, of some length $n$; by $C(n)$ (steps 6-8) there is $g\in S'$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, with $S'_g\to S_g$ an isomorphism [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
